content_identical_across_runs.how: SHA-256 over every table's sorted rows, two runs, same seed

byte_identical_across_runs.how: raw file bytes compared across two runs at the same seed
byte_identical_across_runs.note: False. DuckDB writes non-deterministic file metadata, so the contract is content-identity, which the spec already stated. Kept in the report rather than dropped, because a later DuckDB making it true is worth noticing.

p50_ms.how: wall clock around run_sql, 50 gold SQLs

p95_ms.how: wall clock around run_sql, 50 gold SQLs, 95th percentile

clustering.caveat: The 50 items are 10 clusters of 5 parameterisations, not 50 independent trials. A systematic flaw in one pattern fails all five of its items together, so an interval computed as if n=50 is narrower than the evidence supports. Report alongside the templating disclosure.

gold_set.templating_disclosure: Questions are templated: 10 patterns x 5 parameterisations. That caps how far these numbers generalise to freely-phrased questions, and it is stated on screen rather than left in a footnote.

rule_coverage.caveat: refunds_net is exercised by ONE pattern only (p05_net_revenue, 5 items, 1 cluster). The sweep can therefore make no claim about that rule: with a single cluster there is no independent evidence, and the Phase 3 ablation will show it as unmeasurable for reasons that have nothing to do with the verifier under test. Read a flat refunds_net line as 'not measured here', not as 'the verifier missed it'. Rule enforcement is still covered by the Phase 2 rule-surface probes, which test the verifier directly rather than inferring it from sweep outcomes.

ambiguity.how: Naive variants compared pairwise per item with rows_equal. A collision marks the item partial; it is never dropped or regenerated.

langsmith.dataset_url: REDACTED — a LangSmith dataset URL identifies an organisation
langsmith.dataset_id: REDACTED — see .gitignore for the same decision on _resume_first.log

resumability.plain_english: A 5-item experiment was started, killed after 2 items had been invoked, then restarted against the same experiment name. LangSmith re-invoked all 5 targets, including the 2 that had already completed. The experiment ended with 7 root runs for a 5-item dataset: 2 duplicates, plus 1 run left in "pending" forever because it was in flight when the process was killed. Completed work was neither skipped nor replaced - it was repeated and appended.
resumability.decision: Phase 3 resumes from results/*.json itself. LangSmith is trace-viewing only and must not be relied on to skip completed cells - doing so would double the cost of any interrupted sweep and leave orphaned pending runs in the report.

langsmith.role: ADVISORY ONLY. results/*.json is the system of record. A test runs a cell with the LangSmith client stubbed to raise and asserts the results file is still complete and correct.
langsmith.dataset_scope_note: LangSmith datasets are account-scoped, not project-scoped. LANGSMITH_PROJECT controls where traces and experiment sessions are filed, not where a dataset lives. Re-uploaded under the corrected project setting so future experiment sessions land alongside it.
langsmith.redaction_note: The dataset URL and id were published here and shipped to a public Space by tools/sync_hf.py. They are identifiers, not credentials, and nothing in this repository reads them — results/*.json is the system of record and LangSmith is never consulted for a number. Redacted in place rather than removed so every citation of this file still resolves, which is the same decision recorded in .gitignore for results/_resume_first.log.

findings: L0 clears the cache minimum on no model; its prefix is too short to cache anywhere, so caching cannot reduce sweep cost for this level.

L3 caches on frontier but NOT on worker. This is silent — no error, just a different cost per cell — and it lands directly on the cost comparison, because the cheaper model is the one paying full price for its prefix on every call.
prompts.how: client.messages.count_tokens against each model; no inference run.

rate_limits.how: One minimal request per model via .with_raw_response; every header matching 'ratelimit' plus retry-after recorded verbatim. No loop toward a 429.
rate_limits.note: Pools are per-model. The two models report identical published ceilings, which is not the same as sharing a bucket - remaining counts and reset timestamps move independently, so Phase 3 still caps concurrency per model.

tokens.how: usage fields read off every response, all four classes

by_outcome.how: every call recorded, including failed and timed-out

cost_usd.how: measured token counts x a hand-entered price table (taken 2026-07-29 from https://claude.com/pricing (per million tokens)). Only a billing export would make this a measurement, so the 'est.' label never comes off.
